chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammam, from Sa'id al-Naqqash, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, there is Takbir in al-Fitr (Eid al-Fitr), but it is a prescribed tradition (sunnah).'
I asked: 'Where is it?' He said: 'On the night of Fitr, in the Maghrib and the last 'Isha prayers, and in the Fajr prayer and the Eid prayer, then it is discontinued.'

I asked: 'How should I say it?' He said: 'You say: Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illa Allahu Allahu Akbar, wa lillahi al-hamdu Allahu Akbar 'ala ma hadana. And this is the saying of Allah:'
'And to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] you has guided [you]'

key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)
key_terms.وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ: And to complete the period (referring to fasting)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific time and formula for reciting Takbir on the night of Eid al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the specific timing for the Takbir al-Fitr, restricting it to the Maghrib, last Isha, Fajr, and Eid prayers, thereby establishing a precise liturgical window for this Sunnah. The narration not only provides the verbatim formula but also explicitly grounds the practice in the Quranic command to 'magnify God for His guidance,' highlighting the theological link between ritual completion and divine gratitude. This specification reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the Prophet's household's detailed instructions regarding the temporal boundaries of worship.
